how: Extracted by scripts/gate_shards.py::parse_failures from the six shard logs of the 2026-09-09 six-shard run at 0ffe68a14 (1181 files). That run predates the committed wrapper and is NOT of record for a pass/fail verdict, but its logs are a faithful capture.
provenance_caveat: ⭐ CORROBORATED TWICE, at two different merge-bases. Originally seeded from a run on the branch; corroborated at 78ac8016b, then RE-corroborated at f58383e69 after the rebase. At the new base the two sets are IDENTICAL: master introduced no failure this baseline lacks, and after removing the one entry master FIXED (see removed_because_master_fixed_it, attributed to 4fef130d9) no baseline entry is absent at the base. Nothing here is the hub's. ⛔ If either of the two load-sensitive names recorded under prior_base appears as NEW in a future run, re-run it ALONE before treating it as a regression. 2026-09-10: ChartDrawingOverlay.surfaces.test.jsx was ADDED by the Wave Q1 session, not because Wave Q1 caused it -- it did not -- but because MASTER MOVED and this baseline is a measurement OF master. It is blamed to 8de4da43b (charts Phase 9). Proof, and the third step is the one that counts: it fails at rest alone in 1.4s (so it is not the load-sensitive population); the test and its subject are byte-identical to origin/master; and the same test was RUN on a detached worktree at origin/master with no Wave Q1 code present and failed identically. Left stale, this file would have reported a phantom regression to every branch that ran the gate from now on -- a gate list drifts like any other artifact. 2026-09-10 (2nd): TWO rows REMOVED because MASTER FIXED THEM -- sourcesAreText's NUL bytes and ImportBox.thinkscript's line endings (5e7a88258 'normalise fixture line endings'). ⛔ Removed by measurement, not by hope: both were in the baseline, both are now green in a full run at 591d1a7b7. A baseline that keeps a fixed row makes the next real fix look like a regression's absence.

f58383e69_and_earlier.result: ZERO failures at the base are absent from this baseline (master introduced none), and after the removal below ZERO baseline entries are absent at the base. The two sets are now identical, so nothing in this baseline is hub-introduced.

removed_because_master_fixed_it.attribution_basis: The ONLY master commit between the old base (78ac8016b) and the new one (f58383e69) that touches this test file: 'Wave Q1: the canary's trigger is a measurement, and the write is gated'. Verified an ancestor of f58383e69, and the file passes ALONE at the new base (15/15), so this is a real fix and not a shard-boundary shift.

prior_base.note: Measured 11 files / 12 tests. Two base-only failures there — flowSearchProduct and sharedScreen.route — passed in isolation and were correctly NOT banked; neither fails at the new base either.

corroborated_at_merge_base.7ed6b2ce5: 7ed6b2ce5 (2026-09-10): validated INDIRECTLY, not re-measured. The branch was rebased onto this base and the gate at the rebased HEAD returned no_longer_failing = 0 against these nine names, over a population that grew 1188 -> 1190 -> 1191 as master added test files. The single NEW name was a load-sensitive settle timeout (see load_sensitive) and is not banked. The base measurement was deliberately NOT run: the base tree has 32 fewer test files than the branch, so its shards slice differently and it could not have classified a shard-composition failure either way.

load_sensitive.instruction: ⛔ RE-RUN ALONE BEFORE CLASSIFYING. These names have failed a full sharded run and passed in isolation. A timeout is never banked as permitted breakage — banking one leaves a slot in this baseline that a real failure can occupy unnoticed. None of these is a baseline entry.

Not an assertion -- the body reads and regex-scans every built bundle, tens of MB, which is slow under a loaded six-shard run. ⛔ NOT banked: a timeout in the baseline leaves a slot a real failure can occupy, and this rail's whole job is to catch a real one. ⭐ THE DURABLE FIX IS AN EXPLICIT PER-TEST TIMEOUT on that `it(...)`, because the work is genuinely large -- but the file is a journal-2-0 path and rule 12 assigns it to the Notebook workstream, so it is handed over rather than patched here.

removals.why: It stopped failing in the 2026-09-11T07-36-04 gate. Removed only after confirming it is FIXED and not SILENTLY SKIPPED — the distinction the gate manifest itself asks for. Verified by running the file alone: 12 tests execute and all five of its own planted-cut controls PASS (PLANTED CUT / dynamic edge / worker edge / tracked-vs-untracked orphan / allow-list guards), so the sweep can still detect an orphan. A baseline row left in place for a test that now passes is a slot a real failure can occupy unnoticed.
